selection.method: highest remaining verified actor-primary profiles after Fats Pichon music correction

profiles.name: Simon "Stuffy" Singer
profiles.excerpt: Simon “Stuffy” Singer was a prolific child radio actor before becoming a championship handball player, with hundreds of broadcasts behind him by adulthood.
profiles.bio_html:
Simon Singer was born in Los Angeles in 1941 and began acting professionally as a child under the nickname Stuffy. Radio and television made him a familiar juvenile performer throughout the 1940s and 1950s.

Singer later recalled working in hundreds of radio and television programs with major stars including Jack Benny, Phil Harris, Bob Hope and Eddie Cantor. After leaving acting, he became a national and world champion handball player.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five The Railroad Hour performances credited to Singer, four The Great Gildersleeve appearances, three The Phil Harris-Alice Faye Show broadcasts and additional comedy work.

profiles.name: Will Geer
profiles.excerpt: Will Geer combined stage and radio acting with folk singing and political activism before becoming widely known as Grandpa Walton on television.
profiles.bio_html:
Will Geer was born in Indiana in 1902 and trained in botany before building a life in theatre, radio, film and political activism. His Broadway work stretched across decades, and radio gave him another outlet for serious dramatic performance.

Geer also sang folk music in migrant camps, union halls and political gatherings, often alongside Woody Guthrie and Burl Ives. That work makes singing a genuine second profession within his performance career.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves ten Escape performances credited to Geer, two Gang Busters appearances and additional work on Columbia Workshop and Night Beat.

profiles.name: William Powell
profiles.excerpt: William Powell brought the urbane sophistication of his film career to radio in prestige adaptations and Thin Man-related broadcasts.
profiles.bio_html:
William Powell was born in Pittsburgh in 1892 and became one of Hollywood’s defining sophisticated leading men. His partnership with Myrna Loy in the Thin Man films made Nick Charles one of his most recognizable screen characters.

Powell also appeared frequently on radio in adaptations and star-driven anthology programs. His microphone work drew on the same dry timing and polished delivery that defined his screen persona.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves seven Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Powell, three Screen Directors Playhouse appearances, two The Adventures of the Thin Man broadcasts and additional anthology work.

profiles.name: William Tracy
profiles.excerpt: William Tracy carried a busy film career into radio character work across detective, medical, suspense and Hollywood anthology programs.
profiles.bio_html:
William Tracy was born in Pittsburgh in 1917 and began acting professionally while still young. Stage and film work established him as a lively character actor in pictures including The Shop Around the Corner and Tobacco Road.

Radio used Tracy in a wide range of supporting and featured roles, from Screen Directors Playhouse and Dr. Kildare to Jeff Regan, Investigator and Night Beat.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves three Screen Directors Playhouse performances credited to Tracy, two each on Dr. Kildare, Jeff Regan, Investigator and Night Beat, plus additional dramatic work.

profiles.name: Anne Williams
profiles.excerpt: Anne Williams moved from daytime television into recurring CBS Radio Mystery Theater roles during the 1970s radio-drama revival.
profiles.bio_html:
Anne Williams became familiar to daytime audiences through a long run on Search for Tomorrow, where she played Eunice Martin for roughly a decade.

During the same era, Williams became a recurring performer on CBS Radio Mystery Theater. The anthology format let her move well beyond one soap-opera identity into mystery, suspense and supernatural roles.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 13 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Williams, documenting her substantial participation in the 1970s revival of network radio drama.

profiles.name: Bill Baukum
profiles.excerpt: Bill Baukum was a western-radio supporting actor whose surviving GRH work is concentrated in Wild Bill Hickok and Roy Rogers.
profiles.bio_html:
Bill Baukum is best documented through the western radio repertory of the early 1950s. His surviving credits place him repeatedly in programs built around fast-moving frontier adventure and recurring supporting characters.

Baukum appeared most often on Wild Bill Hickok, with additional work on Roy Rogers. The record supports a professional western-radio profile without requiring unsupported personal details.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 Wild Bill Hickok performances credited to Baukum and one Roy Rogers appearance.

profiles.name: Bill Nighy
profiles.excerpt: Bill Nighy gave one of his major early radio performances as Sam Gamgee in the BBC’s landmark 1981 adaptation of The Lord of the Rings.
profiles.bio_html:
Bill Nighy was born in England in 1949 and built a career across stage, radio, film and television. Long before his later international screen fame, BBC radio gave him a major role in one of its most ambitious dramatic adaptations.

In the 1981 BBC Radio 4 production of The Lord of the Rings, Nighy played Samwise Gamgee opposite Ian Holm’s Frodo. His warm, grounded performance helped anchor the emotional center of the epic adaptation.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 13 installments of The Lord of the Rings featuring Nighy as Sam, documenting an important early chapter of his acting career.

profiles.name: Eleanor Tanin
profiles.excerpt: Eleanor Tanin was a West Coast radio actress whose surviving GRH work is strongest in Gunsmoke and Fort Laramie.
profiles.bio_html:
Eleanor Tanin worked in the professional West Coast radio repertory during the final years of network dramatic broadcasting. Her surviving credits place her especially strongly in adult westerns.

Tanin appeared repeatedly on Gunsmoke and Fort Laramie, with additional work on Escape and Have Gun, Will Travel. Those programs relied on naturalistic supporting actors rather than broad western caricature.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves nine Gunsmoke performances credited to Tanin, two Fort Laramie appearances and additional work on Escape and Have Gun, Will Travel.

profiles.name: Gail Patrick
profiles.excerpt: Gail Patrick moved from a successful acting career into pioneering television production, becoming the executive producer who developed Perry Mason for CBS.
profiles.bio_html:
Gail Patrick was born in Birmingham, Alabama in 1911 and became a major Hollywood character actress during the 1930s and 1940s. Radio extended that screen career through comedy appearances and prestige dramatic adaptations.

After leaving acting, Patrick became one of television’s pioneering women producers. As president of Paisano Productions and executive producer of Perry Mason, she helped develop, sell and oversee the landmark CBS series for nine seasons.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves ten Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Patrick, two Lum and Abner appearances and one Old Gold Comedy Theater broadcast. Her producing career remains a substantial second profession.

profiles.name: Gladys Holland
profiles.excerpt: Gladys Holland was a West Coast radio actress whose surviving work ranges from The Great Gildersleeve and The Whistler to international adventure and crime drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Gladys Holland belonged to the busy West Coast radio repertory of the postwar years. Her surviving credits show a supporting actress moving among comedy, suspense, crime and international adventure.

Holland appeared most often on The Great Gildersleeve, with additional work on The Whistler, A Man Called X, Broadway Is My Beat, Lux Radio Theatre and Rocky Jordan.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves five The Great Gildersleeve performances credited to Holland, two The Whistler appearances and additional broadcasts across several major dramatic series.
